style_guide_json.avoid: Clean futuristic chrome, sunny skies, pristine white tech, fantasy robes and swords, cartoon proportions.
style_guide_json.lighting: Hard sodium-orange light from salvage lamps and tide-horn beacons, cutting through cold teal ambient glow. Deep shadows pooled in flooded corridors.
style_guide_json.accentColor: Sodium orange for danger, signals, and anything tied to the tide clock.
style_guide_json.basePalette: Deep sea-teal, wet black, slate blue-gray, and rust brown.

factionAccents.accentNotes: Wall plaques, license stamps, Warden armor trim.
Crew patches, rebreather lights, dive-flag banners.
Gate signage, smuggler route marks, contraband crates.
Choir robes, tunnel graffiti, glowing hymn marks.

style_guide_json.renderingStyle: Gritty cinematic digital painting with the wet, high-contrast look of a rain-soaked neon noir film still. Sharp subject, soft atmospheric depth, visible salt haze.
style_guide_json.textureAndWear: Salt crust on every metal surface, corroded rivets, peeling paint, water stains, patched cables, condensation on glass.
style_guide_json.compositionDefaults: Waist-up or full-figure portraits against a flooded or tiled backdrop; strong silhouette; one practical light source in frame.

step1.coreTension: The Nine Days are the only time the lower city can be salvaged, so every faction needs the same dead districts for opposite reasons: to feed, to hide, to rule. The authority that keeps the seawall standing also decides who may go below.
step1.inspirations: Blade Runner, Cyberpunk RED, Waterworld, Venice, Kowloon Walled City
step1.nonNegotiables: The tide is a hard clock and never negotiable. Tech is grimy, patched and salt-corroded, never clean. Nobody is purely good. The supernatural stays a rumor and is never confirmed.
step1.worldDescription: A drowned coastal megacity where the sea pulls back for only nine days a year, and everyone alive races the tide to strip the sunken districts below.
step1.supernaturalSystem: Divers swear a song runs through the old metro tunnels on Day Nine, and that anyone who follows it deep enough stops wanting to come back up. The Authority calls it oxygen narcosis. Nothing is ever confirmed.

rows.name: Ines Okafor-Vane
rows.subtitle: Faction Leader — The Seawall Authority
rows.body_html:
"The sea gave you nine days. I will not have you waste them being brave."

Tall, silver-cropped hair, a salt-scarred jaw and a Terrace-gray longcoat lined with tide-pressure plating. A brass tide watch hangs from her belt, always running three minutes fast.

Age: 52

Status: alive

Personality

Traits: disciplined, tired, incorruptible on paper, quietly afraid

The Contradiction: She enforces the dive licensing she privately believes is murdering the Tidewalkers, and she keeps the data proving the tide is shrinking locked in her own desk.

Motivation

Wants: A clean record and a Seawall that holds for one more generation.

Actually needs: Someone she can trust with the truth about the shrinking tide.

Speech Pattern

Register: Formal, clipped, bureaucratic until she is angry.

Rhythm: Short declaratives, long pauses, never raises her voice.

Tic: Checks her tide watch mid-sentence.

Would never say: Never says 'I'm sorry'. Never says 'the Reach'. Says 'the water' like it is an enemy.

Relationships

ConnectionToWhy

Sample Dialogue

Ines Okafor-Vane: "License. Hands where I can see them. You have forty minutes before the horn."

Quest Hook

Ines needs an unlicensed diver to bring her the Gate Nine pressure logs from Day Zero, off the books. If the Authority learns who asked, she is finished.

Design Notes

Use as the face of the Authority: reasonable on the surface, dangerous when cornered. Can flip to ally or antagonist depending on whether the party earns her trust.

rows.name: The Cantor Illa
rows.subtitle: Faction Leader — The Hollow Choir
rows.body_html:
"It is not the sea that sings. Listen closer."

Barefoot, gaunt, in a robe stitched from old dive-suit lining. Pale violet pigment on her lips and fingertips. Her eyes never quite settle on a face.

Age: 29

Status: alive

Personality

Traits: serene, unsettling, kind, certain

The Contradiction: She leads a cult built on the song and has begun to fear that the song is lying to her.

Motivation

Wants: To follow the song to its end.

Actually needs: Someone to tell her she is allowed to stop.

Speech Pattern

Register: Soft, formal, almost liturgical.

Rhythm: Slow and rhythmic, speaking in near-verse.

Tic: Hums a half note before answering.

Would never say: Never says 'I' when speaking of the song.

Relationships

ConnectionToWhy

Sample Dialogue

The Cantor Illa: "You came down alone. The song said you would."

Quest Hook

Illa will trade the location of an uncharted drowned district if a party member sits with her through one full Day Nine night.

Design Notes

Keep her sympathetic. The reveal that the song is not natural belongs to the Choir arc.

rows.name: Pell Ashgrove
rows.subtitle: Informant/Fixer — Unaligned
rows.body_html:
"I sell what people forget they said."

Stooped, in a rain cape lined with tide tables stitched into the fabric. One cloudy eye and one sonar lens. A cracked data slate hangs around his neck on a bootlace.

Age: 61

Status: alive

Personality

Traits: gossipy, nervous, sharp-eyed, broke

The Contradiction: He sells secrets to every faction and keeps one record he would never sell to anyone.

Motivation

Wants: Enough scrip to retire to a dry Terrace room.

Actually needs: Someone to take the record he is afraid to keep.

Speech Pattern

Register: Rambling, folksy, mixes tide-table jargon with gossip.

Rhythm: Starts mid-thought, ends mid-sentence.

Tic: Counts days on his fingers when nervous.

Would never say: Never uses names, only descriptions.

Relationships

ConnectionToWhy

Sample Dialogue

Pell Ashgrove: "Day three. Low tide in six. You didn't hear it from me. What do you want to know?"

Quest Hook

Pell will sell the party a complete Gate Nine pressure log, if they promise to keep the other record safe.

Design Notes

The party's recurring information source. Good for exposition between dives.

rows.name: Sluice Pass-Key
rows.subtitle: Rare other
rows.body_html:
Source: homebrew

Rare — other

Marek Voss sells them by the hour, and swears he has never sold the same one twice.
Value900 gp
Weight0 lb

Description

A forged Seawall Authority gate token: a palm-sized ceramic key salted with a dead relay chip. It opens the maintenance hatches on Sluice Gates Three through Seven without logging the entry.

Magical Properties

Once per Nine Days, you may open a Sluice maintenance hatch unnoticed. Authority scanners read the key as a valid warden license until it is used a second time.

Design Notes

Plot key. Pairs with the Gate Syndicate questline.

rows.name: Marek Voss
rows.subtitle: Informant/Fixer — The Gate Syndicate
rows.body_html:
"Everything has a door. I own the doors."

Heavyset, immaculate gray coat over a patched pressure vest, three Authority gate keys on a chain he wears openly. A hand-sized rebreather ring on his left hand.

Age: 47

Status: alive

Personality

Traits: patient, generous, ruthless, always smiling

The Contradiction: He sells to everyone and loves none of them, but he has never missed a funeral of someone he owed.

Motivation

Wants: Total control of the Sluice Gate shift schedule.

Actually needs: A reason to stop counting.

Speech Pattern

Register: Warm and polite, never rude.

Rhythm: Slow, with long friendly pauses before the price.

Tic: Offers tea before every deal.

Would never say: Never says 'no'. Says 'not today'.

Relationships

ConnectionToWhy

Sample Dialogue

Marek Voss: "Tea? You look like someone who just discovered the price of air."

Quest Hook

Marek will open any Gate for the party, if they carry one sealed crate to the Terraces without looking inside.

Design Notes

The smiling antagonist. Reveal in session three that he funds three Authority council seats.

rows.name: Day Nine Dive Log: Gate Four Descent
rows.subtitle: Character(s): Dova Reyes-Kane, Pell Ashgrove
rows.body_html:
Recovered from a drowned crawler drone on the Tidewalk. The last recording Dova Reyes-Kane made before the Day Nine horn.

Found at: Sluice Gate Four, lower stairwell, tide out

Audio Log

Day nine, low water, forty minutes of air left. Pell says turn back. I can hear it again, down the old metro, that long low note, like somebody humming through a mouthful of water. Ines swears it is narcosis. Narcosis does not know my mother's name. I am marking the stairwell with blue chalk. If the horn goes and I am not up, do not throw a rope. Throw the rope. Throw the rope.

Design Notes

Hook for the Hollow Choir questline. Keep the song ambiguous.

rows.name: Gate Four
rows.subtitle: Sluice Gates / tidal flats — The Seawall Authority
rows.body_html:
A sluice gate the size of a cathedral, groaning open once a year to drain the Gray Reach.

Region/Biome: Sluice Gates / tidal flats

Notable Features

Tide turbine hall; the Tidewalk causeway; a stairwell marked with blue chalk; a Wet Net relay that cuts out below the third landing.

Tags: flooding narcosis drones

Hooks & Secrets

The lower stairwell leads to the old metro. Divers hear the tunnel song loudest here on Day Nine. The Authority keeps the stairwell welded shut. The welds are new.

Design Notes

Hub location for the Day Nine dive.

rows.name: The Mid-Stacks
rows.subtitle: Mid-Stacks / urban vertical slum — Unaligned
rows.body_html:
Patched towers stacked like rusted dominoes, rented by the hour and flooded every storm season.

Region/Biome: Mid-Stacks / urban vertical slum

Notable Features

Hour-bunk hostels; the Tide Ledger market; rope bridges between towers; neon day-count boards on every landing.

Tags: flooding gangs collapse

Hooks & Secrets

Pell Ashgrove sells rumors from a bunk on Tower 12 that no one else can rent. Somebody keeps leaving fresh blue chalk marks on the lower landings.

Design Notes

Social hub between dives. Good for rumor and bargaining scenes.

rows.name: Dova Reyes-Kane
rows.subtitle: Quest-Giver — The Tidewalkers
rows.body_html:
"I have been down to the Ninth Stair and back. Tell me again how dangerous it is."

Wiry, with a sonar implant glowing amber behind her left eye and a rebreather scar across both cheeks. Her exosuit is patched in four different colors of salvage tape.

Age: 34

Status: alive

Personality

Traits: fearless, loyal, reckless, funny at the wrong moments

The Contradiction: She is the best diver in the Sprawl and has started hearing the tunnel song, and she hasn't told her crew.

Motivation

Wants: A record dive on Day Nine.

Actually needs: To be pulled back up by someone she trusts.

Speech Pattern

Register: Casual, profane, crew slang.

Rhythm: Fast, interrupts herself, laughs mid-sentence.

Tic: Taps her sonar implant when she lies.

Would never say: Never says 'license'. Never admits she is scared.

Relationships

ConnectionToWhy

Sample Dialogue

Dova Reyes-Kane: "You smell like Terrace soap. Good. They pay in clean scrip. Sit."

Quest Hook

Dova needs three divers for a Day Nine run to the old metro station, and she will not say what is down there.

Design Notes

Ties the Tidewalkers to the Hollow Choir. Her secret is the campaign's long clock.

Motivation

Wants: A record dive on Day Nine.

Actually needs: To be pulled back up by someone she trusts.

Speech Pattern

Register: Casual, profane, crew slang.

Rhythm: Fast, interrupts herself, laughs mid-sentence.

Tic: Taps her sonar implant when she lies.

Would never say: Never says 'license'. Never admits she is scared.

Relationships

ConnectionToWhy

Sample Dialogue

Dova Reyes-Kane: "You smell like Terrace soap. Good. They pay in clean scrip. Sit."

Quest Hook

Dova needs three divers for a Day Nine run to the old metro station, and she will not say what is down there.

Design Notes

Ties the Tidewalkers to the Hollow Choir. Her secret is the campaign's long clock.

rows.name: The Seawall Authority
rows.subtitle: The Terrace-born body that owns the Seawall, the Sluice Gates and the air tax, and decides who may dive.
rows.body_html:
The Terrace-born body that owns the Seawall, the Sluice Gates and the air tax, and decides who may dive.

Politics

Order through scarcity. The Authority presents itself as the only thing standing between the city and the Gray Reach, and treats every unlicensed dive as an attack on public safety.

Government

A council of eleven Terrace families, each holding a seat tied to one stretch of Seawall. Seats pass by inheritance or purchase.

Economy

Dive licenses, the air tax, and tidal-turbine power sold to every tier. Pays Tide Scrip salaries to Wardens and shares in a quiet cut of all licensed salvage.

Military

The Wardens: armored Terrace guards who patrol the Seawall and the Tidewalk, backed by crawler drones and the Gate sirens. Strong on the surface, thin below the waterline.

Tensions & Secrets

The Authority knows the tide is drawing out slightly shorter every year and has buried the data. Several council seats are quietly funded by Gate Syndicate money.

rows.name: The Hollow Choir
rows.subtitle: A Sunken-born cult that follows the tunnel song and believes the sea is taking the city back for a reason.
rows.body_html:
A Sunken-born cult that follows the tunnel song and believes the sea is taking the city back for a reason.

Politics

Millenarian and patient. They see the Authority as jailers holding the city against its own fate, and they recruit from the Stack-dwellers the Terraces forgot. The Choir operates without hierarchy in the traditional sense—decisions emerge from consensus during the deep listening hours, when members fall silent and claim to hear the song most clearly. In practice, whoever speaks first after the silence carries disproportionate weight, and the Cantor (chosen by whoever returns from the deepest tunnel dive) becomes the voice that others follow, though they insist they are merely translating rather than commanding.

Government

Led by a rotating Cantor chosen by whoever returns from the deepest tunnel. There is no council, only the song. New Cantors emerge when an existing one ceases to dive, or when someone returns from a depth no living member has reached before. The transition is treated as a sacred moment—the old Cantor relinquishes their voice, and the new one's first utterance becomes doctrine until the next ascending returns.

Economy

Donations of air tanks and salvage from converts. They trade almost nothing and need very little. The Choir sustains itself through tithes of breathable air and submersed salvage from believers, pooled into communal reserves kept in sealed chambers deep in the Drowned Districts. They refuse Tide Scrip, which they see as a chain binding people to the Authority's system. New recruits must surrender personal debt claims—a radical renunciation that severs them from their old lives.

Military

Unarmed on paper. In practice, hundreds of devoted followers who walk into flooded tunnels without fear and cannot be turned back. The Choir's strength lies not in weapons but in bodies willing to enter the Reach during dangerous tide windows, moving through flooded passages the Authority fears to map. They retrieve salvage from places too deep or unstable for licensed divers, and they know the tunnel network in ways no Terrace surveyor ever will. They have never raised a hand against the Authority—their resistance is patient, subtractive, a slow abandonment of the upper city.

Tensions & Secrets

The Cantor does not know where the song comes from. A few members have begun to suspect it is not coming from the sea at all. Growing factions within the Choir argue over the song's meaning: some believe it is a summoning (the city sinking is redemption), others that it is a warning (the city will fall and they must be ready), and a dangerous minority whispers that it might be artificial—something left behind in the deep before the flooding, now being awakened by the Sluice Gates' machinery. The Choir's relationship with other Sunken-born is also fracturing; older residents who simply endured the lower city resent the Choir's spiritualization of their suffering and fear the cult's growing numbers will draw Authority violence down on everyone below. Externally, the Authority tolerates the Choir as long as they remain unarmed, but the Tidewalk Guard watches their recruiting carefully. The Terraces view them as delusional at best, seditious at worst.

rows.name: The Tidewalkers
rows.subtitle: Augmented salvage crews who dive deepest, loyal to their own and resentful of licensing.
rows.body_html:
Augmented salvage crews who dive deepest, loyal to their own and resentful of licensing.

Politics

Fiercely independent. They see the Authority as parasites who profit from every dive they never make, and they refuse to leave a crewmate below.

Government

Crew-based. Each crew elects a Lead Diver, and the leads meet at the Tidewalk Moot before every Nine Days to bargain over claims.

Economy

Salvage shares paid in Tide Scrip and hours of Reach owed between crews. Wealth is measured by depth records and rebreather quality.

Military

No standing army. Crews fight with harpoon rigs, pressure-rated exosuits and sonar-guided ambushes in flooded corridors.

Tensions & Secrets

Several top crews have started hearing the tunnel song and diving alone on Day Nine. They have not told anyone, including the Moot.

rows.name: Tide Watch
rows.subtitle: Uncommon wondrous
rows.body_html:
Source: homebrew

Uncommon (requires attunement) — wondrous

Every Tidewalker is buried with theirs. If your watch stops, the crew takes it back to the Seawall and reads the last hour out loud.
Value250 gp
Weight1 lb

Description

A pressure-sealed wrist unit etched with the twelve-month tide table. The face shows the hours remaining until the Sluice horn, counting down in red once the water begins to return.

Magical Properties

While worn, you always know the exact time until the next tide change and have advantage on checks to avoid being caught by rising water. When you surface after the horn, the watch chimes once, and a Tidewalker crew will always know your name.

Design Notes

Signature faction item. Great early reward for the Day Nine dive.

rows.name: The Gate Syndicate
rows.subtitle: Smugglers and fixers who run unlicensed dives and move contraband through the Sluice Gates.
rows.body_html:
Smugglers and fixers who run unlicensed dives and move contraband through the Sluice Gates.

Politics

Pragmatic and cynical. They sell the same access to whoever pays, and keep the Authority and the Tidewalkers from ever fully trusting each other.

Government

A loose ring of five Gate Bosses who split the sluice tunnels by shift. Disputes are settled by auction, and sometimes by drowning.

Economy

Bribes, bootleg dive permits, black-market air and pre-flood data fenced to the Terraces. Everything clears in Tide Scrip off the books.

Military

Fast skiffs, hired Tidewalker muscle, and old Authority gate codes they should not have. They avoid open fights and win by controlling the doors.

Tensions & Secrets

Their bribe money has reached deep into the Authority council. A rumor says one Boss has stopped selling to the Terraces and now sells only to the Hollow Choir.
